q: Features which enable organisms to survive in their environment are called _____
e: Features which enable organisms to survive in their environment are called adaptations. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic. Variations is not adaptations.

q: Adaptations can be classified as anatomical, physiological, or _____
e: Adaptations can be classified as anatomical, physiological, or behavioral. Physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water. Adaptations are inherited traits that help survival in a given environment. Morphological is not behavioral.

q: The presence of closable nostrils in camels is an example of a(n) _____ adaptation.
e: The presence of closable nostrils in camels is an example of a(n) anatomical adaptation. Anatomical adaptations are structural, such as thick fur or a flattened leaf. Behavioral is not anatomical.

q: A camel’s ability to vary its body temperature over 6°C is a _____ adaptation.
e: A camel’s ability to vary its body temperature over 6°C is a physiological adaptation. Physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water. Anatomical is different: anatomical adaptations are structural, such as thick fur or a flattened leaf.

q: Camels lying down together to minimize sun exposure is a _____ adaptation.
e: Camels lying down together to minimize sun exposure is a behavioral adaptation. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome. Physiological is different: physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water.

q: Natural selection is the process by which well-adapted organisms have a greater chance to _____
e: Natural selection is the process by which well-adapted organisms have a greater chance to breed and pass on alleles. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. Mutate is not breed and pass on alleles.

q: The theory of natural selection was first proposed by _____
e: The theory of natural selection was first proposed by Charles Darwin. Darwin's evolution by natural selection is a core theme of biology. Louis Pasteur is not Charles Darwin.
Artificial selection is also called selective breeding. Random mating is not selective breeding.

q: In artificial selection, selection is due to _____
e: In artificial selection, selection is due to human influences. Environmental factors is not human influences.

q: Compared to natural selection, artificial selection is a _____ process.
e: Compared to natural selection, artificial selection is a faster process. Slower is not faster.

q: In artificial selection, inbreeding is common and often leads to _____
e: In artificial selection, inbreeding is common and often leads to loss of vigour. Hybrid vigour is not loss of vigour.
Natural selection may lead to new species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring. Loss of all variation is not new species.
